stem: A patient’s levothyroxine dose was changed today. When should TSH be rechecked?
why_correct: T4’s 7-day half-life means steady state takes about 6 weeks; recheck TSH at 6–8 weeks.
takeaway: TSH after a dose change: 6–8 weeks.
discriminator: Same rule after starting.

E.why: T4’s 7-day half-life means steady state takes about 6 weeks; recheck TSH at 6–8 weeks.

stem: A patient with a family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma asks about semaglutide. Best answer?
why_correct: GLP-1 RAs are contraindicated with personal or family history of MTC or MEN2.
takeaway: GLP-1 RA: GI upset, pancreatitis, gallstones, MTC/MEN2.
discriminator: Weight loss; glucose-dependent, low hypoglycemia.

B.why: GLP-1 RAs are contraindicated with personal or family history of MTC or MEN2.

stem: A patient starting desmopressin for central diabetes insipidus asks what to watch for. Best counseling?
why_correct: Desmopressin keeps free water; the risk is hyponatremia — monitor sodium and limit fluids.
takeaway: DI drug keeps water; SIADH drug lets it go.
discriminator: Tolvaptan: start in hospital (overcorrection).

C.why: Desmopressin keeps free water; the risk is hyponatremia — monitor sodium and limit fluids.

stem: A patient with untreated Graves disease arrives febrile, tachycardic and confused. Correct sequence?
why_correct: Iodine is given only after PTU; giving it first supplies substrate for new synthesis before synthesis is blocked.
discriminator: Steroids blunt conversion and cover adrenal insufficiency.

A.why: Iodine is given only after PTU; giving it first supplies substrate for new synthesis before synthesis is blocked.

stem: A patient on metformin with eGFR 38 is scheduled for a CT with iodinated contrast. What should happen?

distractors.text: Add an SGLT2 the same day

why_correct: Hold metformin for contrast with reduced kidney function (lactic acidosis); avoid when eGFR < 30.
discriminator: Long-term metformin → check B12.

A.why: Hold metformin for contrast with reduced kidney function (lactic acidosis); avoid when eGFR < 30.

E.text: Add an SGLT2 the same day

stem: A patient on octreotide for acromegaly develops right-upper-quadrant pain after meals. Most likely cause?
why_correct: Octreotide/lanreotide: GI upset, gallstones and bradycardia.
discriminator: Octreotide also treats variceal bleeding and carcinoid.

E.why: Octreotide/lanreotide: GI upset, gallstones and bradycardia.

stem: Which class carries the highest hypoglycemia risk among oral agents, and why?
why_correct: Sulfonylureas close K-ATP channels and release insulin regardless of glucose.
discriminator: Older adults who fall → avoid sulfonylureas.
src: L08 S11; S14; S35; SG U4-R11; SG U4-M

C.why: Sulfonylureas close K-ATP channels and release insulin regardless of glucose.

stem: Which pairing of drug and mechanism in Cushing syndrome is correct?
why_correct: Ketoconazole blocks several steroidogenic CYPs; metyrapone the last cortisol step; mifepristone the glucocorticoid receptor; spironolactone the mineralocorticoid receptor.
discriminator: Receptor blockers leave hormone levels high.

A.why: Ketoconazole blocks several steroidogenic CYPs; metyrapone the last cortisol step; mifepristone the glucocorticoid receptor; spironolactone the mineralocorticoid receptor.

stem: Why is PTU preferred over methimazole in thyroid storm?
why_correct: PTU blocks synthesis and peripheral conversion — a faster effect on active hormone.
discriminator: Propranolol and steroids also blunt conversion.

B.why: PTU blocks synthesis and peripheral conversion — a faster effect on active hormone.

stem: A patient on chronic prednisone ran out of refills; now hypotensive, weak and confused. Best management?
why_correct: Adrenal crisis from abrupt withdrawal after HPA suppression — immediate IV hydrocortisone and fluids.
discriminator: Hydrocortisone has mineralocorticoid action too.

C.why: Adrenal crisis from abrupt withdrawal after HPA suppression — immediate IV hydrocortisone and fluids.

stem: A patient with Parkinson disease on high-dose cabergoline needs monitoring for which serious effect?
why_correct: High-dose cabergoline (Parkinson doses) is linked to valvulopathy; lower prolactinoma doses carry less risk.
takeaway: Cabergoline: twice weekly; high dose → valves.
discriminator: Nausea and orthostasis are common.

A.why: High-dose cabergoline (Parkinson doses) is linked to valvulopathy; lower prolactinoma doses carry less risk.

stem: A 74-year-old living alone with a prior fall needs an add-on to metformin. Best class?
why_correct: Low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk; sulfonylureas force glucose-independent insulin release, raising fall risk.
discriminator: Match the drug to the patient’s risk profile.

A.why: Low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk; sulfonylureas force glucose-independent insulin release, raising fall risk.

stem: Five weeks into methimazole, a patient has fever and a sore throat. What should happen?
correct: Stop it and check a CBC
why_correct: Thionamides carry an agranulocytosis boxed warning; fever or sore throat → stop and check a CBC.
discriminator: Risk is highest in the first 90 days (textbook).

B.text: Stop it and check a CBC
B.why: Thionamides carry an agranulocytosis boxed warning; fever or sore throat → stop and check a CBC.

stem: A patient on repaglinide starts gemfibrozil for triglycerides. What should be anticipated?
why_correct: Gemfibrozil raises repaglinide levels (CYP2C8) — hypoglycemia risk.
discriminator: Skip the dose if the meal is skipped.

E.why: Gemfibrozil raises repaglinide levels (CYP2C8) — hypoglycemia risk.

stem: A man on finasteride for BPH has a PSA of 1.9 ng/mL. How should it be read?
why_correct: Finasteride lowers PSA by about half — double the value when screening.
discriminator: Pregnant women must not handle crushed tablets.

A.why: Finasteride lowers PSA by about half — double the value when screening.

stem: A patient starting a 3-month prednisone course asks how to take it. Best counseling?

distractors.text: At bedtime on an empty stomach
Double doses if you miss one

why_correct: Take in the morning with food; consider bone and GI protection; taper chronic therapy.
discriminator: Watch glucose, mood, infection.

A.text: Double doses if you miss one

B.text: At bedtime on an empty stomach

D.why: Take in the morning with food; consider bone and GI protection; taper chronic therapy.

stem: Why does long-term exogenous hormone therapy suppress the gland above it?
why_correct: The peripheral hormone feeds back on the hypothalamus/pituitary, turning the levels above it down.
takeaway: Give a hormone → the axis above it quiets.
discriminator: Same logic: levothyroxine lowers TSH; prednisone lowers ACTH.

A.why: The peripheral hormone feeds back on the hypothalamus/pituitary, turning the levels above it down.

stem: An 82-year-old with coronary artery disease is newly hypothyroid. How should levothyroxine start?
why_correct: Older adults and cardiac patients start low and titrate slowly to avoid angina or arrhythmia.
takeaway: Old heart → start low, go slow.
discriminator: Over-replacement: AF and bone loss.

A.why: Older adults and cardiac patients start low and titrate slowly to avoid angina or arrhythmia.

stem: A woman on tamoxifen for breast cancer starts paroxetine for hot flashes. What is the concern?
why_correct: Paroxetine and fluoxetine inhibit CYP2D6 and blunt tamoxifen activation.
discriminator: Report vaginal bleeding on tamoxifen.

B.why: Paroxetine and fluoxetine inhibit CYP2D6 and blunt tamoxifen activation.

stem: A patient on amiodarone develops thyroid dysfunction. What should be expected after stopping it?
why_correct: Amiodarone can cause hypo- or hyperthyroidism; it persists after stopping because of its very long half-life.
discriminator: About 3% develop thyrotoxicosis (textbook).

D.why: Amiodarone can cause hypo- or hyperthyroidism; it persists after stopping because of its very long half-life.

stem: A conscious patient on insulin has glucose 55 mg/dL. What first?
correct: 15 g fast carbs, recheck in 15 min

distractors.text: Give the next insulin dose early

why_correct: Rule of 15: 15 g carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes; glucagon or IV dextrose for severe cases.
discriminator: Beta-blockers mask warning signs.

A.text: Give the next insulin dose early

D.text: 15 g fast carbs, recheck in 15 min
D.why: Rule of 15: 15 g carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes; glucagon or IV dextrose for severe cases.

stem: A patient with SIADH stays hyponatremic despite fluid restriction. Tolvaptan is chosen. Key safety step?

distractors.text: Give with salt tablets at home

why_correct: Tolvaptan can overcorrect sodium (osmotic demyelination) and injure the liver — start in hospital.
takeaway: SIADH: fluid restriction first, then tolvaptan or demeclocycline.
discriminator: Demeclocycline: photosensitivity, nephrotoxicity.

A.text: Give with salt tablets at home

B.why: Tolvaptan can overcorrect sodium (osmotic demyelination) and injure the liver — start in hospital.

stem: A patient with NYHA class III heart failure needs diabetes therapy. Which drug is contraindicated?
why_correct: TZDs cause fluid retention and are contraindicated in NYHA class III–IV heart failure.
discriminator: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart-failure events.

D.why: TZDs cause fluid retention and are contraindicated in NYHA class III–IV heart failure.

stem: A patient on levothyroxine starts an oral contraceptive. What change should be anticipated?
why_correct: Estrogens raise thyroid-binding globulin, so levothyroxine needs rise — check TSH.
discriminator: Inducers (rifampin) also raise needs.

D.why: Estrogens raise thyroid-binding globulin, so levothyroxine needs rise — check TSH.

stem: After thyroidectomy, a patient has perioral numbness, low calcium and low PTH. Mainstay therapy?
why_correct: PTH activates vitamin D; calcitriol bypasses that step — given with oral calcium.
takeaway: Low PTH → calcitriol + calcium; watch hypercalcemia.
discriminator: Recombinant PTH 1-84 if refractory.

B.why: PTH activates vitamin D; calcitriol bypasses that step — given with oral calcium.

stem: A patient with acromegaly is started on pegvisomant. Which lab tracks the response?
why_correct: Pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor so IGF-1 falls; GH rises and is not used to monitor it.
discriminator: Pegvisomant doesn’t shrink the tumor — check liver tests too.

D.why: Pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor so IGF-1 falls; GH rises and is not used to monitor it.

stem: A patient on insulin and propranolol has glucose 48 mg/dL without tremor or palpitations. Why?
why_correct: Beta-blockers can mask hypoglycemia warning symptoms.
takeaway: Insulin + beta-blocker → check glucose, not symptoms.
discriminator: Rule of 15: 15 g carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes.

C.why: Beta-blockers can mask hypoglycemia warning symptoms.

stem: A patient with Cushing syndrome on ketoconazole starts simvastatin. What is the concern?
why_correct: Ketoconazole: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation and strong CYP3A4 inhibition.
discriminator: Azoles also raise corticosteroid exposure.

E.why: Ketoconazole: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation and strong CYP3A4 inhibition.

stem: Which statement about tamoxifen and raloxifene is correct?
why_correct: Tamoxifen activates the endometrium (cancer risk); raloxifene blocks it; both raise VTE.
discriminator: CYP2D6 inhibitors blunt tamoxifen.

D.why: Tamoxifen activates the endometrium (cancer risk); raloxifene blocks it; both raise VTE.

stem: A patient with Addison disease on hydrocortisone has low BP and high potassium. What should be added?
why_correct: Primary adrenal insufficiency needs mineralocorticoid replacement alongside a glucocorticoid.
discriminator: Monitor BP and potassium.

C.why: Primary adrenal insufficiency needs mineralocorticoid replacement alongside a glucocorticoid.

stem: A woman on levothyroxine takes it with her calcium and iron at breakfast; her TSH is high. Best advice?
why_correct: Calcium, iron and antacids reduce absorption; take levothyroxine 30–60 minutes before breakfast, 4 hours apart.
takeaway: Levothyroxine timing matters as much as dose.
discriminator: Recheck TSH 6–8 weeks after any change.

C.why: Calcium, iron and antacids reduce absorption; take levothyroxine 30–60 minutes before breakfast, 4 hours apart.

stem: What shared concept links thyroid-storm sequencing and diabetes drug choice?
correct: Where in the pathway a drug acts
why_correct: Knowing exactly where a drug acts determines both its efficacy and its specific risks.
takeaway: Position in the pathway = benefit and risk.
discriminator: Same idea: iodine after PTU; no sulfonylurea in a faller.

B.text: Where in the pathway a drug acts
B.why: Knowing exactly where a drug acts determines both its efficacy and its specific risks.

stem: A patient on semaglutide asks to add sitagliptin. Best answer?
why_correct: Do not combine a GLP-1 RA with a DPP-4 inhibitor — same incretin pathway.
discriminator: GLP-1 RA: weight loss; DPP-4: weight neutral.

C.why: Do not combine a GLP-1 RA with a DPP-4 inhibitor — same incretin pathway.

stem: How does combined hormonal contraception prevent ovulation?
why_correct: Exogenous estrogen + progestin feed back to suppress GnRH pulses and FSH/LH — no follicle, no LH surge; progestin thickens mucus.
takeaway: The same feedback template as Session 1.
discriminator: >99% effective with perfect use.

E.why: Exogenous estrogen + progestin feed back to suppress GnRH pulses and FSH/LH — no follicle, no LH surge; progestin thickens mucus.

stem: Which drug–site pairing for glucose lowering is correct?
why_correct: β-cell: sulfonylureas, meglitinides; liver: metformin; muscle/fat: TZDs; kidney: SGLT2; gut/incretin: GLP-1 RA, DPP-4.
takeaway: Place each class on the map.
discriminator: Incretin drugs are glucose-dependent.

E.why: β-cell: sulfonylureas, meglitinides; liver: metformin; muscle/fat: TZDs; kidney: SGLT2; gut/incretin: GLP-1 RA, DPP-4.

stem: A patient on haloperidol develops galactorrhea and a high prolactin. What explains it?
why_correct: Antipsychotics and metoclopramide raise prolactin by blocking dopamine’s inhibitory brake.
discriminator: Avoid unmonitored antipsychotic changes with dopamine agonists.

C.why: Antipsychotics and metoclopramide raise prolactin by blocking dopamine’s inhibitory brake.

stem: A patient with asthma is in thyroid storm. Which drug choice needs caution?
why_correct: Propranolol is avoided in asthma and decompensated heart failure; it blunts symptoms and conversion.
discriminator: Avoid aspirin for fever — it frees bound hormone.

E.why: Propranolol is avoided in asthma and decompensated heart failure; it blunts symptoms and conversion.

stem: Which insulin is the only one given intravenously?
why_correct: Only regular insulin is given IV; rapid-acting goes with meals, regular 30 minutes before.
discriminator: Glargine is never mixed with other insulins.

E.why: Only regular insulin is given IV; rapid-acting goes with meals, regular 30 minutes before.

stem: Which glucocorticoid is the most potent relative to hydrocortisone?
why_correct: Potency vs. hydrocortisone: prednisone about 4×, dexamethasone about 25–30×.
takeaway: Dexamethasone: potent, long-acting, little salt retention.
discriminator: Hydrocortisone has mineralocorticoid action too.

D.why: Potency vs. hydrocortisone: prednisone about 4×, dexamethasone about 25–30×.

stem: How does cinacalcet lower PTH?
why_correct: Cinacalcet makes the CaSR more sensitive so the gland reads calcium as high and lowers PTH.
discriminator: Nausea, hypocalcemia, QT; CYP2D6 inhibitor.

D.why: Cinacalcet makes the CaSR more sensitive so the gland reads calcium as high and lowers PTH.

stem: A patient on long-term metformin has numb feet and macrocytic anemia. What should be checked?
why_correct: Long-term metformin causes B12 deficiency (impaired ileal uptake) — monitor B12.
discriminator: Same with long-term PPIs (Unit 3).

E.why: Long-term metformin causes B12 deficiency (impaired ileal uptake) — monitor B12.

stem: A woman with galactorrhea and amenorrhea has a prolactinoma. First-line therapy?
why_correct: Dopamine agonists restore dopamine’s inhibitory brake on prolactin; cabergoline is twice weekly and better tolerated.
discriminator: Antipsychotics and metoclopramide raise prolactin.

E.why: Dopamine agonists restore dopamine’s inhibitory brake on prolactin; cabergoline is twice weekly and better tolerated.

stem: Which insulin is cloudy with variable absorption and a peak at about 4–10 hours?
why_correct: NPH is an intermediate-acting suspension with variable absorption.
takeaway: Sort insulins: rapid, short, intermediate, long.
discriminator: Glargine must not be mixed with other insulins.

B.why: NPH is an intermediate-acting suspension with variable absorption.

stem: Why do SGLT2 inhibitors increase genital yeast infections?
why_correct: Blocking renal glucose reabsorption raises urinary glucose, favoring fungal overgrowth.
takeaway: Glucose in the urine = fuel for yeast.
discriminator: Also euglycemic DKA — hold when ill or before surgery.

B.why: Blocking renal glucose reabsorption raises urinary glucose, favoring fungal overgrowth.

stem: A patient with Graves disease is in thyroid storm and on long-term prednisone. What extra role do steroids play?

distractors.text: They have no role in storm

why_correct: Corticosteroids blunt peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion and cover relative adrenal insufficiency.
discriminator: Chronic steroid users also need stress coverage.

A.why: Corticosteroids blunt peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion and cover relative adrenal insufficiency.

E.text: They have no role in storm

stem: A dialysis patient with high PTH starts cinacalcet. What must be monitored?
why_correct: Cinacalcet sensitizes the CaSR so PTH and calcium fall; monitor for hypocalcemia (and QT).
discriminator: Cinacalcet inhibits CYP2D6.

A.why: Cinacalcet sensitizes the CaSR so PTH and calcium fall; monitor for hypocalcemia (and QT).

stem: A patient on spironolactone for hyperaldosteronism also takes lisinopril. What should be monitored?
why_correct: Spironolactone blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor; ACEi/ARBs and potassium add to hyperkalemia.
discriminator: Gynecomastia is the other classic effect.

B.why: Spironolactone blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor; ACEi/ARBs and potassium add to hyperkalemia.

stem: A woman at 9 weeks’ gestation has Graves hyperthyroidism. Which drug is preferred now?
why_correct: PTU is preferred in the first trimester (methimazole teratogenic); switch to methimazole after.
discriminator: PTU carries the greater liver risk.

C.why: PTU is preferred in the first trimester (methimazole teratogenic); switch to methimazole after.

stem: A 37-year-old who smokes daily asks for hormonal contraception. Which choice fits?
why_correct: Smoking at 35+ substantially raises estrogen’s thromboembolic risk; progestin-only methods avoid it.
takeaway: Smoker ≥ 35, migraine with aura, VTE → progestin-only.
discriminator: Rifampin and other inducers → backup method.

C.why: Smoking at 35+ substantially raises estrogen’s thromboembolic risk; progestin-only methods avoid it.

stem: A patient on empagliflozin is admitted for surgery and is vomiting. What should happen?
why_correct: SGLT2 inhibitors risk volume depletion and euglycemic DKA — hold when ill or before surgery.
takeaway: Sick day or surgery → hold SGLT2.
discriminator: Genital yeast infections; rare Fournier gangrene.

D.why: SGLT2 inhibitors risk volume depletion and euglycemic DKA — hold when ill or before surgery.
